self_assessment: Added openlibrary/solr/utils.py holding the Solr shared state (solr_base_url, solr_next) and the moved load_config, get/set_solr_base_url, get/set_solr_next, the SolrUpdateState dataclass (with __add__, has_changes, to_solr_requests_json, clear_requests) and the solr_update / solr_insert_documents helpers, verbatim so their retry and 400-response handling is unchanged. update_work.py now imports all of them from the new module instead of defining them, and its imports of dataclasses, httpx exception types, openlibrary.config and utils.retry - orphaned by the move - were dropped. update_edition.build_edition_data no longer needs its function-local import of get_solr_next from update_work (the cyclic import that motivated the refactor); it imports it at module level from solr.utils. index_subjects.py now takes solr_insert_documents from solr.utils and only build_subject_doc from update_work. Because update_work re-exports the names, scripts/solr_updater.py's update_work.set_solr_base_url/set_solr_next keep working and mutate the utils globals. Verified: openlibrary/tests/solr/ produces the identical set of 46 failures before and after the change (all pre-existing conftest/pytest incompatibilities in this environment), imports of all four modules succeed, the re-exported names are the same objects as the ones in solr.utils, and a scratch script exercised SolrUpdateState's merge/serialize/clear plus the solr_next setter.
